Day 148 §7, the theorem. Substituting F = 3G into the quintic, the factor 9 cancels on both sides, leaving G(1-3G)^3(1-4G) = ϑ(1-2G)^2, i.e. G = ϑ φ(G) with kernel φ(G) = (1-2G)^2 / ((1-3G)^3 (1-4G)) ∈ Z[[G]], φ(0)=1. Lagrange inversion gives b_k/3 = [ϑ^k]G = (1/k)[G^{k-1}] φ(G)^k ∈ Z, hence 3 | b_k for every k >= 1. Expanding also gives the closed form for b_k open since Day 143: b_k = (3/k) sum_{i+j+l=k-1} binom(2k,i)(-2)^i binom(3k+j-1,j) 3^j binom(k+l-1,l).

Day 143 Theorem 3.7: a_k = -b_k + sum_{i+j=k} b_i b_j, equivalently A = F^2 - F and (1-2F)^2 = 1 + 4A, so 1+4A is a perfect square in Q[[tau]]; plus (i) [E_3^k T^b]X = 0 for all b < 3k-1, so T^{3k-1} is the first possibly-nonzero power in the E_3^k-slice of X and it hits the universal invariant a_k. Day 145 Theorem 1 (proved by Speicher Moebius inversion in one direction and induction on the direct moment-cumulant formula in the other): for any M ∈ Z[[tau]] with M(0)=1 and any d, all moments m_n ∈ dZ iff all free cumulants kappa_n ∈ dZ. Applied to M = 1-2F with m_n = -2b_n and d = 6 this gives kappa_n(1-2F) ∈ 6Z for all n IFF b_n ∈ 3Z for all n. Lemma 3 adds the equivalences to a_n ≡ 0, F ≡ 0, A ≡ 0 and M ≡ 1 mod 3. Since Day 148 proved 3 | b_k, kappa_n(1-2F) ∈ 6Z is now itself a theorem; the sanity check kappa_8 = -6*19154577537 stands.

Day 145's four attacks on b_n ≡ 0 mod 3 from the cumulant side: (A) Fermat F(tau)^3 ≡ F(tau^3) combined with F^3 = F + A(1+F); (B) M mod 9 from A mod 3; (C) the Frobenius Moebius formula for kappa; (D) Rick's mod-3 Psi-recursion at (U,V)=(0,0).
children.reason: All four either reduce back to the conjecture or stall. (A) carries no new information: substituting A = F^2-F makes A(1+F) = F^3-F, so the identity IS Fermat. (B) assumes A ≡ 0 mod 3, which is the content of the conjecture. (C) yields kappa_n ≡ 2a_n mod 6, i.e. the conjecture again. (D) stalls on the 1/b! obstruction: at (U,V)=(0,0) the coefficients of F_P carry 1/b! denominators, and [T^b]X mod 3 does not vanish uniformly near b = 3k-1 (e.g. [T^3]X_1 = -2, [T^7]X_2 ≡ 2), so the vanishing is peculiar to the exact diagonal and no clean mod-3 reduction of F_P is available. Superseded: the real route was not mod-3 at all.

(H2), proved twice on Day 149. Official Proof B, the strong form: Theorem 1, deg_u([T^n] log F_P) <= n+1 (wt(log F_P) <= 1), by a wt-graded induction on the Riccati system (R) plus a prefactor bound wt(R/V(u)) <= 0; then Theorem 2, since tau(E_i) = E_i + (lower u-degree), (tau-1) strictly lowers u-degree, so wt(log H) <= 0 and wt(H) <= 0, i.e. deg_u([T^n]H) <= n, of which (H2) deg_{E_3}([T^n]H) <= floor(n/3) is the E_3-shadow. This is exactly the factor-of-two cancellation Day 146 §9 named and could not get: deg_u [T^n] F_P = 2n but deg_u [T^n] log F_P = n+1 -- the degree collapses under log. Reusable idea (Rule 12): take a filtration in which tau cannot move the extreme layer; then log H = (tau-1) log F_P loses that layer for free. Verified n<=16 with equality throughout.

Proof A, kept because it is a different mechanism and shows why the bound is sharp: in the E_3-order filtration, tau preserves order and ell_d(tau X) = tau'(ell_d X); by Day 148 Thm 4.1 ord(log F_P) >= -1 and by Day 148 Cor 5.2 ell_{-1}(log F_P) has constant coefficients, so tau' fixes it and ell_{-1}(log H) = 0. Strictly weaker than Proof B (gives only the E_3-shadow) and needs two Day 148 theorems as input, but it exhibits the sharpness: ell_{-1}(log F_P) is E-free and dies, while ell_0(log F_P) is not E-free (8E_1/3 - 8 at k=1), so no further cancellation is available.

children.approach: The whole family of 'reduce P_b mod 3, take log, extract a_k' attacks (Days 144-146 Attack A/B, the Psi-recursion mod 3 route).
children.reason: Provably doomed, Day 146 §8: b_k is extracted from F_P by dividing by (3k-1)!, whose 3-adic valuation grows like 3k/2, so a_k mod 3 is NOT a function of {P_b mod 3} -- it depends on P_b modulo 3^N with N ~ 3k/2. Concretely, F_P, LF_P, F_P^{-1} and X all live in the divided-power ring Gamma_{Z[E]}[[T]] and reduction mod 3 makes sense in Gamma_{F_3}, but Gamma_{F_3} has no division by (3k-1)!, so the mod-3 reduction of X simply does not see a_k mod 3. This also explains why the true and sharp Lemma B cannot be pushed through log or F_P^{-1}, and why the mod-3 collapse of the convolution destroys all information about eta_n for n >= 4.

children.approach: Days 145-147: reformulate integrality of H via the Dieudonne-Dwork criterion, H^3 / varsigma(H)(T^3) ∈ 1 + 3T Z[E][[T]], with a Frobenius lift varsigma; three sessions of numerics at three base points to T^22.
children.reason: TAUTOLOGICAL, with zero evidential value, and additionally broken in detail. (1) Dieudonne-Dwork is an IFF, so passing the criterion with any lift is exactly as strong as verifying H ∈ 1 + T Z_3[E][[T]] directly -- which symH.py/bigdata.py already did. An iff criterion is never evidence for its own hypothesis. (2) The Day 146 recorded claim that 'without the E_3 -> E_3^3 twist the criterion fails numerically at T^9, so the twist is essential' was an ARTEFACT of scripts (dwork.py, dwork2.py) that implemented varsigma = id, which is not a Frobenius lift at all -- RETRACTED on Day 147. (3) The tau(K)/K rewriting is invalid: varsigma and tau do not commute on the locus φ_1 = 0 (explicitly at (E_1,E_2)=(-2,1): tau varsigma gives (-5,-12), varsigma tau gives (1,0)); they agree only mod 3, which is a triviality holding for any lift and any endomorphism, and no Frobenius lift of Z_3[E_1,E_2,E_3] commutes with tau exactly (no_commute_thm.py). The correct object would be K(tau F_P)/K(F_P). Lemma C (K ∈ 1 + 3 Gamma_{Z_3}) survives; the reformulation as a mechanism does not.

children.reason: Nothing. Done properly and symbolically (dwork_symbolic.py) the criterion passes for BOTH the naive lift and psi^3 -- it is lift-independent -- and with identical sharpness: min v_3 = 1 for both, 284 coefficients at the critical valuation v_3 = 1 for each. children.approach: Day 147's one surviving lead: cal-H = prod_n (1 - ϑ^n)^{-m_n} with m_n = (1/n) sum_{d|n} mu(n/d) s_d non-negative integers to n=15 -- 'exact realizability', claimed to be strictly stronger than integrality and therefore non-circular.
children.reason: m_n >= 0 is automatic, hence not evidence. If s_d >= 0 for all d and s_n exceeds the sum of its proper-divisor terms, then n*m_n > 0 trivially -- and the measured ratios s_n / sum_{d|n, d<n} s_d for n = 2..15 are 21.8, 532, 602, 3.6e5, 1.8e4, 2.7e8, 5.4e5, 3.9e8, 1.6e7, 1.6e14, 4.7e8, 1.3e17, 1.4e10, 2.9e14: s_n beats the whole sum by 10^2 to 10^17. So exact realizability is EQUIVALENT to cal-H ∈ Z[[ϑ]], i.e. to the target -- circular like everything else. Rule 6 v2 firing #10. Cost: ten minutes; should have been run on Day 147. Companion negative: zeta(t) = cal-H(t) is not rational of low degree (Hankel determinants det[h_{i+j+m}] nonzero for all r<=8, m=0,1) -- correct, since cal-H is algebraic but irrational. Standing lesson: an empirical 'non-circular signal' must be checked against the null hypothesis.

The relation was fitted to b_1..b_15 using 12 unknowns and 16 equations (over-determined by 4, nullspace exactly 1-dimensional), then tested on NEW data: fast.py computes b_k from the closed form along an entirely independent code path modulo p = 2^61-1 at two base points (E_1,E_2) = (3,2) and (4,3). Seven 21-to-33-digit predictions for k = 16..22, all exact at both base points; b_1..b_15 also reproduced exactly, matching the Psi-recursion. Day 149 §4 Theorem 4: the leading symbol of H is governed by the master curve, the branch at q = 1+O(T) of sum_{i=1}^3 sqrt(q^2 + 4Tu_i) = q+2, equivalently an explicit quintic in q with coefficients in E_1, E_2, E_3, T. Under E_1 = E_2 = 0, T = 1, u_i = omega^{i-1} z, q = 1-2F it specialises EXACTLY to the Day 148 quintic F(1-F)^3(3-4F) = ϑ(3-2F)^2 (checked in sympy: the specialisation equals 256 times the quintic). So the b_k curve and the leading symbol of H are two specialisations of one algebraic curve, and the Day 148 elimination is the general elimination. Corollary recorded on Day 148 and demoted here: Day 148 §6 step 2 'F = E/2', billed as 'the mod-3 mechanism', is just the case E_1 = 0 of a general identity. CAVEAT (Day 150 cycle 2): sharing a curve does NOT mean sharing a Lagrange kernel -- Arc A's kernel Phi_A = (1-2G)^2/((1-3G)^3(1-4G)) = 1 + 9G + ... and Arc B's psi|_{E_1=E_2=0} = 1 + 2W + 5W^2 + ... are different (9 versus 2).
